newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China Steel raises April-June prices.
newsitem.headline: China Steel raises April-June prices.

text.p: China Steel Corp, Taiwan's largest steelmaker, said on Friday it has decided to raise prices of its three steel products in the second quarter of 1997 to reflect local and international market trends.
The firm will raise the price of low-carbon bar rod to T$11,450 per tonne from T$11,050 in the first quarter, it said in a statement.
It will also raise the price of steel plates to T$12,000 per tonne from T$11,800 and the price of electronic galvanised coil to T$17,600 per tonne from T$17,000.
China Steel will keep the price of hot-rolled sheets, cold-rolled sheets and electric sheets unchanged at T$10,350, T$13,350 and T$16,300 per tonne, respectively, it said.
China Steel's price adjustment was seen as a key indicator for domestic steel product prices, analysts said.
